fields.h1: Build Social Media Automation for Every Post Your Team Ships
fields.hero_description: Build social media automation that routes each draft for sign-off, then posts it to Instagram and LinkedIn on time.
fields.features_heading: What Social Media Automation Takes Over
fields.features_subheading: Social media automation runs the repeat work around each post. Deciding what is worth saying stays with your team.
fields.feature_1:
One calendar feeds every network

Instagram and LinkedIn posts sit in one table, one row each with the image, caption, and time slot. The app publishes every row through that network's API and saves the live link.
fields.feature_2:
Captions drafted from your own notes

An AI step turns a product note or a blog link into a first-draft caption in your house style. A writer edits every draft before it enters review. Nothing reaches a feed unread.
fields.feature_3:
Review rules your brand lead writes

Drafts reach the brand lead in Slack. Captions that name a price or a giveaway go to legal as well. Each approval is stored on the post with the approver's name and a timestamp.
fields.feature_4:
Publishing limits counted per account

Instagram allows 100 API-published posts per account in any 24-hour window. The app counts every account's posts against that limit and holds anything past it for the next window.
fields.feature_5:
Evergreen posts back in the queue

Rows tagged Evergreen return to the queue 90 days after they ran, with a fresh caption for review. Rows tagged Seasonal are retired for good once their date has passed.
fields.feature_6:
Your posting rules, exported as code

The calendar, review rules, and weekly report export to your GitHub on paid plans. Adding a network or a new reviewer takes one prompt, and the code behind it stays in your hands.

fields.tab_content_1:
Every approved row in the calendar goes live on time

The content calendar lives in Airtable, one row per post. At each slot, a post marked Approved with an image attached is published to the brand's Instagram professional account, and the post link is saved to the row. A row still in Draft is held, and the social lead gets a Slack message.
fields.tab_content_2:
Captions that mention a price wait for a second reviewer

Each draft reaches the brand lead as a Slack direct message. A caption that mentions a price or a discount then goes to legal. Approve moves the post into the publishing queue. Request changes sends it back to the writer with the comment attached, and the row records who decided and when.
fields.tab_content_3:
New listings go to Instagram once the agent signs off

When a listing's status changes to Active in the brokerage's database, the app drafts a carousel from its first 5 photos, the price, and the open house time. The listing agent approves the draft from a phone. The post then goes to the brokerage's Instagram and its LinkedIn company page.
fields.tab_content_4:
Monday's report flags the weakest post of the week

Every Monday at 8:00 AM, the app pulls reach and interactions for last week's Instagram and LinkedIn posts into one table. Engagement rate is interactions divided by reach. The report lands in #marketing with the posts ranked, and any post under 2% is marked for the team to review.

fields.howto_title: How to Build Social Media Automation
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to settle what you post and who approves it, then connect your accounts and test social media automation.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Audit what you post each week
fields.howto_step_1_des: List every network and account you post to, who writes for each, and how many posts go out in a normal week. Note where posts stall today: waiting on an image, a caption or someone's sign-off.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Decide the columns every post needs: network, slot, image, caption, status, and owner. Emergent builds the calendar as a table in your own database. The team can then sort it by week or by writer.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Say who signs off on each kind of post, in plain sentences. Routine posts need the brand lead. Anything with a price, a contest, or a customer's photo also goes to legal. Those sentences become the routing the app follows.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Connect each Instagram professional account and LinkedIn company page through their APIs, plus Slack for reviews. Start with one Instagram account and one week of posts, then add the other networks once that week runs clean.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Set slots for each network from your own analytics, not a generic best-time chart. A tea shop's followers may scroll before work; a brokerage's buyers may browse on Sunday evening. The queue fills those slots in the order rows were approved.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Point the app at a test Instagram account for the first few days. Check that carousels keep their photo order, captions keep their line breaks and every post link lands in the right calendar row before switching to the live account.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Once posts publish on their own, add the weekly report. Watch which formats earn saves and comments, then give those formats more slots. A format that trails the rest for four straight weeks loses its slot.

The 5-5-5 rule: comment on five people's posts, respond to five stories and send five thoughtful direct messages, about 15 minutes a day
